question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$M=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{13} & \sqrt{17} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $M-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
M-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{13}-\lambda  & \sqrt{17} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(M-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}\sqrt{13}-\lambda  & \sqrt{17} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (\sqrt{13}-\lambda )(\frac{1}{2}-\lambda )-0\cdot \sqrt{17} & =0 \\ (\lambda -\sqrt{13})(\lambda -\frac{1}{2}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =\sqrt{13}$ and $\lambda =\frac{1}{2}.$

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are the entries on the main diagonal.
